column1: # India, in.karachi: Dawat-e-Islami's city cards (rulings R193 and R194, the Pakistan lane of 13 Nov 2026; pk-dawateislami.tsv has
# the cards' own account). Ten Indian cities' cards for November 2026 are held (the private archive only: paths and the app's own
# coordinates here, never a printed time; Delhi's Sehar and Iftar card for Ramadan 1448, once held, has a script-style address on
# record and no record of how it was asked; it is out until the owner rules on it: ruling R237). On the method alone the app began a prayer a
# minute before the city's card in nine of them: Delhi (Asr under the Hanafi school on 22 days of 30, Dhuhr on 17, Isha and the
# standard Asr on some), Hyderabad and Bengaluru (Maghrib), Bengaluru (Fajr on 3 days), Mumbai (Isha), Kolkata (Asr under the
# Hanafi school on 2 days), and Chennai, Pune, Jaipur and Ahmedabad (the review of 13 Nov 2026: Asr under the Hanafi school at all
# four, on 12, 21, 18 and 3 days of 30, with Dhuhr, Isha or Fajr on some days at each of the first three and Fajr on 2 days at
# Ahmedabad). Those nine are units by their own cards (SouthAsia.indiaCards), each row naming its unit (`in.karachi/<unit>`): eight
# at the app's own point for the city, the fit rows below; Delhi's card within Delhi's unit beside Dawat-e-Islami's Delhi table
# (in-karachi.tsv), its rows the unit's own (`in.karachi/delhi`) at the table's point and at every app point within the unit, and
# past the unit as far as the table's bound (in-dawateislami-envelope.tsv). Since four cards of four more cities were early again,
# an Indian place with no card held takes the latest margins the nine held cards ask (ruling R194, indiaBeyondCards). Lucknow's
# card is held out, with no unit: the one Indian card the rule was not made from, and the rule covers it.
# F is the card's Fajr at the minute at or after its seconds (a start), E the same time at the minute at or before them (the end
# of eating: the card prints one dawn), S its sunrise at the minute at or before, the rest starts.
